summary: The App Control policy must add the signing certificate as a trusted publisher in the User Mode Signing Scenario, shown with an example SiPolicy XML. The policy should be signed so Ansible, which usually runs as Administrator, cannot remove it with tasks like win_file or win_regedit.
questions: How do I add my signing certificate as a trusted publisher in a WDAC policy?
Why should the App Control policy be signed when using Ansible?
Which signing scenario should the Ansible certificate go into?
Could an Ansible task disable my App Control policy?

answer_card.title: Trusting the Ansible signing certificate in App Control
answer_card.answer_md:
Add the certificate as a trusted publisher under the **User Mode Signing Scenario** (`ID_SIGNINGSCENARIO_UMCI`), for example:

```text
<Signers>
   <Signer Name="Some Signer" ID="ID_SIGNER_S_0">
      <CertRoot Type="TBS" Value="..." />
      <CertPublisher Value="Some Publisher" />
   </Signer>
</Signers>
...
<SigningScenario ID="ID_SIGNINGSCENARIO_UMCI" FriendlyName="User Mode Signing Scenario" Value="12">
   <ProductSigners>
      <AllowedSigners>
         <AllowedSigner SignerId="ID_SIGNER_S_0" />
      </AllowedSigners>
   </ProductSigners>
</SigningScenario>
```

Then apply the policy. **Warning:** Ansible usually runs as Administrator, so sign and apply the policy in a way that a task such as `win_file` or `win_regedit` can't unset it.
